item.description: We've updated our GitHub math repo with 6 new Lean formalizations, 19 modifications, and 3 withdrawals. The repo now has ~42% top-line results formalized. We will continue to update the repo with … (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: State of Devs 2026 survey results: developers are feeling exhausted
item.description: I just published the results for this year's State of Devs developer survey, which covers topics such as career, health, worldview, and even hobbies. (2 sources: javascriptweekly, rprogramming)

item.title: Meta and Microsoft take steps to reduce employee usage of Claude AI
item.description: Meta and Microsoft are implementing new measures to limit employee use of Claude AI—discover what this means for the future of AI in the workplace. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: On using AI as a writing assistant
item.description: Some people are using AI for writing assistance, but not everyone is using it the same way. (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Cloudflare Open Sources Decision Models for AI Agents
item.description: During its recent “Birthday Week”, Cloudflare announced Clef, a set of open-weight AI models designed to choose between predefined options rather than generate text. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Presentation: Multi-Agent Patterns from Spotify’s AI Powered Advertising Platform
item.description: Pratik Rasam discusses how Spotify Ads Manager runs production-grade multi-agent systems at scale using Google ADK Java. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Navier-Stokes lost in translation: Why Lean verification of AI autoformalisation does not guarantee correct natural language proofs
item.description: Autoformalisation is increasingly used to verify mathematical texts, including those generated by AI, as in OpenAI's announced proof of blow-up of solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations. (1 source: lobsters)
